newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarians increase their support for NATO -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Hungarians increase their support for NATO -- poll.

text.p: The proportion of Hungarians backing NATO membership has risen significantly one month ahead of an alliance summit expected to invite new members, Hungary's defence ministry said on Thursday.
The July 8-9 summit in Madrid is widely expected to invite Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to open accession talks later this year, with Romania and Slovakia also in the running.

A nationwide opinion poll conducted for the Hungarian Ministry of Defence in the first week of June showed 61 percent of the population backed NATO membership compared to 47 percent in March, ministry spokeman Lajos Erdelyi told Reuters.
He attributed the increase to greater public awareness after a government campaign to explain the issue.
"If the citizens have enough information to choose this shows they can do so," he said.

The proportion of those opposing NATO membership remained roughly the same, at 27 percent, according to the survey by the Hungarian Gallup Institute. Twelve percent of the 1,800-strong sample were undecided, down from 26 percent.

The campaign to sell NATO included a heavily publicised air show last month in Keskemet in central Hungary to which a chartered train, the "NATO Express", carried politicians, journalists, military leaders, diplomats and foreign defence contractors.
"The public has received a lot of information through the media and the air show and the NATO Express certainly helped," Erdelyi said.
Fifty percent of those polled said they saw joining NATO as cheaper than neutrality.

This was a message the government tried to hammer home during its campaign as it pursues controversial plans to re-equip the Hungarian air force with $1 billion worth of new fighters, probably Western ones.
Thirty-four percent thought staying out of NATO would be cheaper.
Ministry State Secretary Matyas Eorsi said on Wednesday the government was committed to holding referendums on both NATO and EU membership, but that it was too early to say when they would be held.
